checks.title: Every statement has its source
checks.what: Each cover, rule, benefit, number, obligation and deadline cites the articles it comes from, and each cited or referred article is in the model.
checks.why: A decision is only as good as its source. With the article on every statement, a person can check each step of a decision against the document.

findings.text: Art. 304 uses Art. 204.3, Art. 204.4, Art. 204.5, Art. 204.6, Art. 204.8, Art. 204.9: 7 rules of the model are the same rules, with Art. 304 among their sources.
Art. 407 uses Art. 204.3, Art. 204.4, Art. 204.5, Art. 204.6, Art. 204.8, Art. 204.9: 7 rules of the model are the same rules, with Art. 407 among their sources.
171 statements cite 90 of the 141 articles of the model.

checks.title: The product overview is complete
checks.what: For every cover and every vehicle class, the model says whether the cover is basic, an option, or not insurable.
checks.why: A gap in the overview is a claim that nobody can decide: is the cover in the policy or not?

findings.text: 25 covers × 3 vehicle classes: each has exactly one status (basic, option or not insurable).

checks.title: The certificates agree with the product
checks.what: Each certificate answers every fact of a certificate, and includes an option only where the product overview offers it, with its module.
checks.why: The General Conditions say what each module covers; the certificate says what one policy has. A decision is wrong when it reads one as the other.

findings.text: Example: a passenger car with partial casco, collision, accident and Help Point PLUS: complete. Modules: accident insurance, partial casco, collision (full casco), third party liability.
Every module and option, for a passenger car: complete. Modules: legal protection, roadside assistance, accident insurance, partial casco, collision (full casco), third party liability.

checks.title: No dead questions, no dead rules
checks.what: Every question of the claim check is needed by a rule or a calculation, and every rule can apply in at least one situation.
checks.why: A question that no rule needs wastes the user's time. A rule that can never apply is a mistake in the model, or in the document.

findings.text: All 32 questions of the claim check are used, and all 57 rules can apply in at least one situation.

checks.title: No contradictions between statements
checks.what: For each thing that the statements name (tyres, Europe, gross negligence…), the check compares the statements that cover it with the statements that exclude it. If their covers overlap and their conditions can hold together, the document must say which one wins.
checks.why: A person reads one article at a time. The model sees all statements about the same thing at once, so it finds where two articles say opposite things about the same claim.

findings.text: Roadside assistance in Europe: “Roadside assistance Europe within Europe” (Art. 406) and “Roadside assistance only in Switzerland and Liechtenstein” (Art. 3) can apply in the same situation, with opposite effects.
findings.resolution: Art. 3 says that roadside assistance is valid only in Switzerland and Liechtenstein; Art. 406 extends roadside assistance Europe to Europe as set out in Art. 3. We read the sentence of Art. 3 as about roadside assistance CH/FL.

findings.text: Outside the territorial scope: “Accidents in other people's vehicles: worldwide, for six weeks” (Art. 301.3) and “Outside the territorial scope” (Art. 3) can apply in the same situation, with opposite effects.
findings.resolution: Art. 301.3 says that this insurance applies worldwide, for up to six weeks after leaving the territory.

findings.text: Gross negligence: “Coverage for gross negligence: no reduction of collision benefits” (Art. 202.2) and “Gross negligence: reduced by the degree of fault” (Art. 203.7) can apply in the same situation, with opposite effects.
findings.resolution: Art. 202.2: if the option is agreed, Zurich does not reduce collision benefits for gross negligence.

findings.text: Breakage and wear: “Collision as the consequence of breakage or wear” (Art. 202.1) and “Operation, breakage, wear, wrong handling, lack of oil or coolant, the load” (Art. 204.1) never apply in the same situation. Their conditions keep them apart.

Water and floods: “A natural hazard of the list” (Art. 202.3 c) and “Driving into water: damage due to the operation of the vehicle” (Art. 204.1) can apply in the same situation, with opposite effects.
findings.resolution: Art. 202.3 c covers damage as a direct consequence of high water and floods; Art. 204.1 excludes damage due to the operation of the vehicle. The document does not say where a vehicle that is driven into water belongs. We read it as damage due to operation, as the usual practice does: the water did not come to the vehicle, the driver drove into it.

findings.text: Tyres: “Puncturing the tyres” (Art. 202.3 f) and “Damage only to the tyres or the batteries” (Art. 204.1) can apply in the same situation, with opposite effects.
findings.resolution: Art. 202.3 f covers punctured tyres; Art. 204.1 excludes damage only to the tyres. The document does not say which one wins. We read the closed list of vandalism as the specific rule, so it wins.

checks.title: Repeated statements agree
checks.what: When the document states the same number or benefit in two places, the values must be the same.
checks.why: Documents grow by copy and edit. Two places that state the same limit can drift apart, and then the claim depends on which article the reader found first.

findings.text: An insurance year that counts is stated 2 times, and the statements agree (Art. 6.1: 11; Art. 5: 11).
Onward journey after the loss of keys (Roadside assistance Europe) is stated 2 times, with different values (Art. 406.7: 2000; Art. 406.7: no limit).
findings.resolution: Art. 406.7 lists the onward journey and accommodation twice: once without a limit, once up to 2000 CHF. We apply the limit of 2000 CHF: an item without a limit would make the limited item useless.

checks.title: The compensation table is consistent
checks.what: The table has one row for each year of service, and the share of the catalogue price never goes up.
checks.why: The engine calculates every total loss from this table. One wrong row changes the payment of every claim in that year.

findings.text: 7 years, from 100% to 40%: the share never goes up, so a total loss never pays more for an older vehicle.

checks.title: The test claims give the expected decisions
checks.what: Each test claim is walked as the app does: one question at a time, only the questions that can still change the decision. The status, the cover, the rules and the payment must be the expected ones.
checks.why: The test claims are the specification. When a change to the model changes a decision, a test claim shows it before a user does.
